subject: Variance issue?  issue with loadings : mIRT non-comp, 2 factor model

messages.author: ad66ed17b7874a09
messages.subject: Variance issue?  issue with loadings : mIRT non-comp, 2 factor model
parts:
Hi Phil,

I am running a non-comp model, from a Q-matrix. How do I define the parameters to set the variance to 1?

My model is defined as follows:
Q <- matrix(c(1,1,1,.5,1,0,0,1,
              0,0,0,.5,0,1,1,0), ncol=2, dimnames = list(NULL, c('Factor1', 'Factor2')))

COV <- matrix(c(FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE), 2)

model.Q <- mirt.model(Q, COV=COV)


My results look fine, other than the factor that is allowed to load on both items..
Q.res.c0<-mirt(rev, model=model.Q, guess=0, theta_lim=c(-3.5,3.5),theta_angle = seq(0, 90, by=10), method="MHRM", SE.type="SEM") #mirt w Q-matrix, fix Guessing

coef(Q.res.c0)

$V3
           a1 a2    d1     d2
par     1.473  0 0.436 -2.670
CI_2.5  1.266 NA 0.294 -2.894
CI_97.5 1.681 NA 0.578 -2.446

$V4
           a1    a2    d1     d2
par     4.814 4.281 5.337 -1.457
CI_2.5  2.384 2.266 2.741 -1.815
CI_97.5 7.244 6.296 7.933 -1.098

Thanks,
Emma

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Variance issue? issue with loadings : mIRT non-comp, 2 factor model
parts:
Hi Emma,

This actually seems pretty reasonable to me given my experience with these models (there's a reference in the help files regarding these). It really isn't surprising that the standard errors are so large, and that the intercepts grow to be large as well since these models are extremely unstable, and interchangeable (i.e., fungible). It's one of the reasons I claimed that these models need tens of thousands of participants in order to get any kind of decent parameter confidence range. 

That isn't to say that they are useless, far from it since they still outperform other methods for recovering θ, just that population values are going to be incredibly hard to find.

Phil
